questions.prompt: What phase shift occurs when light reflects from a boundary to a higher refractive index?
questions.answer:
The reflected wave undergoes a half-cycle phase shift:
\[
\Delta\phi=\pi
\]

questions.prompt: At normal incidence, what is the optical path difference for reflection from the two surfaces of a film of refractive index \(n\) and thickness \(t\)?
questions.answer: \[\n\Delta=2nt\n\]

questions.prompt: For reflected light with exactly one reflection phase reversal, state the dark condition.
questions.answer: \[\n2nt=m\lambda_0\n\]

questions.prompt: A film has \(n=1.40\) and \(t=120\,\mathrm{nm}\). Find \(2nt\).
A soap film in air has one phase reversal. Is a film with \(t\to0\) bright or dark in reflected light?
questions.answer: For \(t\to0\), the path contribution is nearly zero, but one reflected ray has a \(\pi\) phase shift. The reflected waves are out of phase, so the film is dark.

questions.prompt: A film with one phase reversal has \(n=1.50\). Find the minimum nonzero thickness for reflected darkness at \(\lambda_0=600\,\mathrm{nm}\).
questions.answer:
For one phase reversal, reflected dark requires
\[
2nt=m\lambda_0
\]
The minimum nonzero thickness uses \(m=1\):
\[
t= rac{600\,\mathrm{nm}}{2(1.50)}=200\,\mathrm{nm}
\]

questions.prompt: A coating has \(n=1.25\). Find the quarter-wave thickness for \(\lambda_0=500\,\mathrm{nm}\).
questions.answer: \[\nt=\frac{\lambda_0}{4n}=\frac{500\,\mathrm{nm}}{4(1.25)}=100\,\mathrm{nm}\n\]

questions.prompt: For reflected light with zero or two phase reversals, state how the bright and dark conditions compare with the one-phase-reversal case.
questions.answer:
With zero or two phase reversals, reflected bright occurs for
\[
2nt=m\lambda_0
\]
and reflected dark occurs for
\[
2nt=\left(m+ rac12ight)\lambda_0
\]
These are swapped relative to the one-phase-reversal case.

questions.prompt: An oil film \((n=1.45)\) floats on water \((n=1.33)\) in air. Count the reflection phase reversals for reflected light.
questions.answer: At the air-oil boundary, reflection is from lower to higher index, so there is a \(\pi\) shift. At the oil-water boundary, reflection is from higher to lower index, so there is no \(\pi\) shift. There is exactly one phase reversal.

questions.prompt: For the oil film in water with one phase reversal, find the minimum nonzero thickness for reflected brightness at \(\lambda_0=580\,\mathrm{nm}\).
questions.answer:
With one phase reversal, reflected bright requires
\[
2nt=\left(m+ rac12ight)\lambda_0
\]
The minimum thickness uses \(m=0\):
\[
t= rac{\lambda_0}{4n}= rac{580\,\mathrm{nm}}{4(1.45)}=100\,\mathrm{nm}
\]

questions.prompt: A film has \(n=1.33\), \(t=250\,\mathrm{nm}\), and one phase reversal. Which reflected vacuum wavelengths are dark for integer \(m\)?
questions.answer:
For reflected dark with one phase reversal,
\[
2nt=m\lambda_0
\]
Thus
\[
\lambda_0= rac{2nt}{m}= rac{2(1.33)(250\,\mathrm{nm})}{m}= rac{665\,\mathrm{nm}}{m}
\]
Visible candidates require checking integer \(m\). For \(m=1\), \(665\,\mathrm{nm}\) is visible; higher orders are ultraviolet or shorter visible only if within range.

questions.prompt: A film has \(n=1.33\), \(t=250\,\mathrm{nm}\), and one phase reversal. Which reflected vacuum wavelengths are bright?
questions.answer:
Bright reflection requires
\[
2nt=\left(m+ rac12ight)\lambda_0
\]
so
\[
\lambda_0= rac{665\,\mathrm{nm}}{m+1/2}
\]
For \(m=1\), \(\lambda_0\approx443\,\mathrm{nm}\), which is visible. For \(m=0\), \(1330\,\mathrm{nm}\) is infrared.

questions.prompt: A film in air has \(n=1.20\) on glass \(n=1.50\). Determine whether reflected dark uses \(2nt=m\lambda_0\) or \(2nt=(m+1/2)\lambda_0\).
questions.answer:
At air-film, reflection is lower to higher index: one \(\pi\) shift. At film-glass, reflection is also lower to higher index: another \(\pi\) shift. There are two phase reversals, so they cancel relatively. Reflected dark uses
\[
2nt=\left(m+ rac12ight)\lambda_0
\]

questions.prompt: Design an anti-reflection coating for glass \(n_g=1.50\) using coating index \(n_c=\sqrt{n_g}\). Find \(n_c\) and the quarter-wave thickness for \(550\,\mathrm{nm}\).
questions.answer:
\[
n_c=\sqrt{1.50}=1.225
\]
For a quarter-wave coating,
\[
t= rac{\lambda_0}{4n_c}= rac{550\,\mathrm{nm}}{4(1.225)}=112\,\mathrm{nm}
\]

questions.prompt: Explain why a film can be bright in reflection and dark in transmission for the same wavelength.
questions.answer: For lossless films, energy redistributed away from reflected light appears in transmitted light. The two reflected rays and the transmitted rays have different phase relationships, so a wavelength suppressed in reflection is enhanced in transmission, and vice versa.

questions.prompt: A wedge-shaped air film lies between two glass plates. Explain why fringes of equal thickness appear, and predict how fringe spacing changes if the wedge angle increases.
questions.answer:
The air-film thickness varies with position, so the condition \(2nt=m\lambda\) is met at repeated positions. For a wedge \(t\approx x\alpha\), adjacent thickness changes require fixed \(\Delta t\), so
\[
\Delta x\propto rac{1}{\alpha}
\]
A larger wedge angle gives closer fringes.

questions.prompt: For a film with one phase reversal, derive the reflected bright and dark conditions from phase difference.
questions.answer:
The round-trip optical phase is
\[
 rac{2\pi}{\lambda_0}(2nt)
\]
One reflection phase reversal adds \(\pi\). Thus
\[
\Delta\phi= rac{4\pi nt}{\lambda_0}+\pi
\]
Bright reflection requires \(\Delta\phi=2\pi q\), giving
\[
2nt=\left(q- rac12ight)\lambda_0
\]
which is \((m+1/2)\lambda_0\). Dark reflection requires \(\Delta\phi=(2q+1)\pi\), giving \(2nt=m\lambda_0\).

questions.prompt: A film thickness is slowly increased from zero. For reflected light with one phase reversal, describe the sequence dark/bright/dark in terms of \(2nt\).
questions.answer:
At \(2nt=0\), reflected light is dark. The first bright condition is
\[
2nt= rac12\lambda_0
\]
The next dark condition is
\[
2nt=\lambda_0
\]
The sequence alternates every additional half wavelength of optical path.

questions.prompt: A film is designed to cancel \(550\,\mathrm{nm}\) reflected light at normal incidence. Explain why it does not cancel all visible wavelengths.
questions.answer: The destructive condition fixes optical thickness relative to one wavelength. For another wavelength, the same \(2nt\) corresponds to a different phase difference. Therefore only a band around the design wavelength is strongly suppressed, not the whole visible spectrum.

questions.prompt: A film is between media with indices \(n_a<n_f<n_b\). Prove which reflected condition is dark and explain the limiting case as \(t\to0\).
questions.answer:
At the top boundary \(n_a	o n_f\), reflection is lower to higher index, so there is a \(\pi\) shift. At the lower boundary \(n_f	o n_b\), reflection is again lower to higher index, so there is another \(\pi\) shift. The relative reflection phase shift is zero, so reflected darkness requires the path phase to be \(\pi\):
\[
2nt=\left(m+ rac12ight)\lambda_0
\]
As \(t	o0\), the reflected rays are in phase rather than out of phase, so the film is not dark by phase cancellation.
